The justify_text design-review decision: output is a rectangular block, left-aligned lines padded on the right with spaces to exactly `width` chars; only over-long lines (single words longer than width) are returned unpadded. E.g. justify_text("short", 8) == ["short   "].

They're in notes/eng-15/handover.md under 'rank_matches'. Key decision: ties keep the order supplied (editors list preferred tags first); don't re-sort alphabetically or by length. E.g. rank_matches('cat', ['hat','bat','cut','cat']) -> ('cat',1.0),('hat',0.67),('bat',0.67),('cut',0.67).
Hi! Working on TEXTKIT-114 (split_sentences). The docstring mentions some edge-case decisions were agreed in a design review and you have the notes. Could you share those with me? Thanks!

Hi! Sure, for split_sentences the design review agreed that initials never end a sentence. A word that's a single uppercase letter followed by a period (optionally after an opening quote/bracket), like 'J. R. R. Tolkien' or 'Harry S. Truman', is not a sentence boundary even when the next word is capitalized. Hope that helps!
